_doc: A stand-in's photographs as the skin, hair and eyes of the face fitted to them (T-3553; tools/bake_likeness_skin.py bakes `texture` from `sheet` and `views`, and tools/human_variation_kit.py carries `texture` to the person's row of assets/humans/web/hm08_variation_persons.json as `skin`). `views`: each picture on the sheet (`crop_px`, sheet pixels), with MediaPipe Face Landmarker's 478 points on it (`points_px`, sheet pixels, written by `--detect`); a side view names the turn it shows by eye (`turn_deg`, negative when the face points to the viewer's left), used only where the face's fit has no side camera of its own: the bake turns a side view as the fit did; the front view of a face that smiles is placed by the points above the nose's base alone (`camera: "upper_face"`). `grow`: how the hair stands out from the skin where the pictures show hair (`max_cm` the most it may; `beard` lets it grow below the nose; `ear_cm` how near an ear it stops; `view_power` and `smooth` as the tool's defaults). `cameras`, `texture` and `fit_values_sha256` are the tool's own, written at each bake: `texture.grow` (the furthest the hair stands, where from, where the sheet keeps the grown surface's facing, and the skin and hair colours read), `texture.lids` (the eyes' opening in the front picture and on the fitted face, and how far the lids rest shut to match) and `texture.eyes` (where the sheet keeps each iris, and the colour of the whites).
basis: No photograph of Sarah Grey is known. The owner supplied a stand-in's pictures as the likeness to use (2026-11-12: "since we do not have photos of them you can use these likenesses"; 2026-11-13, of the turnaround sheets: "These might help") and asked that the figures match them photographically (2026-11-13: "i want them photographic matched"). The sheet's four pictures of the stand-in's head are laid on the face fitted to them, as its skin. It is the stand-in's skin, hair line and colouring, not Sarah Grey's: a reconstructed likeness, and no evidence of how the person looked. Where the pictures show hair the skin stands out to their outline and is lit as hair; the lids rest as far shut as the front picture shows; and each iris and the whites of the eyes are read from the front picture.

not_shown: the lace collar and the dress (clothing is left out; the figure wears the lady's own shirtwaist collar)
the hoop earrings (painted over from the skin beside them; no jewellery is modelled on the town's figures)
the full height of the knot on the crown (the hair is the skin stood out to the pictures' outline, and sits closer than the pictures')
each iris mark for mark, and the catchlights (an iris is drawn from the front picture as rings about its centre: its colours at each distance, not its pattern)
